source_tools.relevance: Exact reactant match and solvent/yield comparison

key_findings.finding: Methanol-associated yields ranged from 73.2% to 78.1% at 100 °C for 5 hours. The highest was 78.1% with a cyclohexyl phosphine/palladium acetate catalyst representation and cesium carbonate; a 77.4% record used triphenylphosphine/palladium acetate and potassium acetate.

source_tools.relevance: Retrieved yield, solvent, temperature, time, and catalyst/base fields

key_findings.finding: One closely matching record used methanol with hydroxide base and triphenylphosphine/palladium acetate, giving 76.3%; another used sodium hydroxide with the same catalyst representation and gave 73.2%. Thus, among the retrieved evidence, methanol is the only directly supported solvent and is the evidence-based choice, but the records do not establish that it is intrinsically superior to THF or DMF because those solvents were not observed.

source_tools.relevance: Directly supports methanol/NaOH and methanol/KOH records and absence of THF/DMF among returned records

key_findings.finding: The returned records do not contain an explicit dppf/iron-containing palladium catalyst representation.
